nodes.recap: chapter header + the ordeal begins: five more days south, food and water gone, motors weakening
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 20          |
-------------------------------


$CThe minisub runs south for five more days.##

You keep to a few meters below the surface, since the motors, whatever
they were built for, were never meant to push a hull through open air.#
They groan and falter the moment the hatch breaks water, and running
submerged is the only way to make any real distance at all.##

By the second day the last of your food is gone.# Theo takes to diving
with a fishing spear scavenged from the wreck, guided by Efeliah, who
can feel the shape of every living thing moving through the dark water
around you and calls it out to him before he goes under.# The catch,
when there is one, is thin and strange and eaten raw.# More often there
is no catch at all.##

The water lasts a little longer than the food, rationed out in careful
sips, but not much longer.# Then it, too, is gone.##

Hour by hour the motors seem to hold less charge than they did at the
start, and the minisub's pace bleeds away with them.# You wonder, in
the quiet, whether you survived everything behind you only to starve
to death in an ocean with no name, thousands of kilometers from
wherever it is you are actually going.##

You lie in the cramped metal berths built into the hull, saving your
strength, saying little, because there is little worth saying.

nodes.recap: your turn at the helm - required verb holds course; optional flavor object gated on lostDayAtSea
nodes.text:
It's your turn at the controls again.##

Efeliah's shift before yours left her folded into the pilot's seat,
utterly absorbed in the flat, uniform blue beyond the polymer nose of
the minisub, as if the water itself might answer a question she hasn't
asked aloud.# Now it's you holding the wheel steady, the compass
needle your only proof that you're going anywhere on purpose at all.##

More than once you're sure you hear voices, low and urgent, somewhere
behind you in the hull.# Every time, it turns out to be stomachs,
yours included, complaining loudly about a meal that never comes.##

Night has stopped meaning anything different from day.# Sleep, when it
comes, does not rest you.

objects.answer:
You keep your hand steady on the wheel and your eyes on the needle,
the only thing in this whole dark ocean that seems to know where
it's going.# Somewhere behind you, someone's stomach growls, long
and mournful, and for a moment you could swear it was a voice
calling your name.

condition.refusal:
You try to count the days and lose the thread almost immediately.#
Six, you think.# Maybe seven.# It stopped mattering a while ago.

objects.answer:
You try to count the days backward and the number keeps coming out
wrong.# You keep forgetting the one you spent chasing the wrong
bearing, the one that cost you clean water before this ordeal had
even properly started.# Call it six days at sea.# Really it's seven,
if you're honest about it.

nodes.recap: the call changes: sixth day, half-conscious, hears it far stronger, urging and afraid - no invented quote, source stays indirect - then Land!
nodes.text:
$CIt happens on the sixth day, in one of those long stretches where
you can no longer tell if you're asleep or only failing to be awake.##

You hear it again.# The voice you had half convinced yourself you
only imagined, long before any of this, before Ayonn, before the
desert, before any of it.# It is louder now than it has ever been,
and it will not stop calling your name, insistent in a way that feels
like it can no longer afford not to be, urging you, somehow, not to
give up.##

And for the first time, underneath the urgency, you feel something
else in it.# Something you would not have expected from a presence
that has never once sounded anything less than certain of itself.##

Fear.##

You don't know whose voice it is, or what it wants, or why it has
been finding you since the day a thunderstorm dropped you onto this
planet with no shoes on.# But you understand, with a clarity that
startles you, that you are not permitted to stop now.# You have to
keep going until you learn the answer.##

That clarity is worth something.# It's just enough to drag you back
to the surface of yourself in time to hear Smiurl, shouting with
whatever strength he has left:##

$Y"Land!"$C

nodes.recap: grounding on the beach, dragging themselves up, collapsing under the trees
nodes.text:
$CWithin the hour the minisub grounds itself on a sandy bottom, most of
its hull breaking the surface at a shallow angle.# You claw the hatch
open and drag yourselves out and up a gentle slope of the finest,
whitest sand you've ever felt, one body length at a time, until the
sand simply receives you and you cannot make yourself move again.##

You don't so much fall asleep as stop being conscious, there in the
shade of broad-leafed trees crowding the edge of the beach, oddly
like the palms of the world you used to live on.

nodes.recap: waking on the beach to Theo and Corolla - water found, game mentioned but not yet explained (rifle payoff moves to node 6)

dialogues.precomment:
You wake to find Theo and Corolla standing over you, and for a
moment you can't work out how much time has passed, or whether any
of this is real.
dialogues.line: We found water.

There's a lovely little stream a few hundred meters that way.# I
even managed to wash.# And we've got a bit of game, too...
dialogues.comment: She trails off, one hand resting on the laser rifle at her hip.

nodes.recap: the rifle payoff for c15's award (corollaArmed) - gated optional object; a fallback verb always advances so nobody gets stuck
nodes.text:
You sit up too fast and your head spins.# Whatever they've found,
you want it, immediately and without conditions.

condition.refusal:
Whatever brought down dinner, Corolla isn't explaining it right
now, and you're too hungry to insist.

objects.answer:
"This laser rifle isn't just an honorific," she finishes, patting
it once.##

The memory arrives before you can stop it: the stage in Ayonn, the
crowd, the moment they pressed that very rifle into her hands.# It
feels like it happened to somebody else, in another life, and your
stomach seizes so hard and so loudly that everyone within ten feet
of you hears it.##

"Give it to me raw, whatever it is, or I swear I'll die right here,"
you say, after drinking for what feels like a full minute straight.

actions.answer:
You drink long and hard, then tear into whatever they've managed
to cook, not particular anymore about how well done it is.

nodes.recap: daytime exploration of the tropical beach, hills behind, sunset
nodes.text:
$CAfter you've eaten, you go exploring, and the place turns out to be
somewhere worth exploring.# Every angle of it looks like a postcard
from a tropical beach back on Earth, the kind that used to make you
roll your eyes in a travel agency window.# The air is warm and
gentle, carried on a light sea breeze, and the water stretches blue
to the horizon, arriving mild and unhurried at the sand, probably
kept that way by a reef somewhere just offshore.##

Behind you, low hills rise thick with vegetation, and every so
often a call comes out of it that is unmistakably an animal and
unmistakably not from anywhere you know, unsettling in a way you
can't quite name.##

You walk one direction and then the other until the sun starts to
sink, setting the sea on fire with a thousand small orange
reflections.# You lie down by the fire Efeliah has going, grateful,
for once, simply to be alive, and wait for Theo, Smiurl and Corolla
to come back with dinner.

nodes.recap: flavor choice while waiting for dinner - both converge, at minimum different text
nodes.text:
There isn't much to do but wait, and watch the fire find its
rhythm.

choices.desc: Watch the flames and let your mind empty out.
Try to place the animal calls coming from the hills.

nodes.recap: flavor branch A
nodes.text:
You watch the flames for a long time, until your thoughts stop
being about anything in particular.

nodes.recap: flavor branch B
nodes.text:
You spend a while trying to guess which of the sounds from the
hills belongs to which invisible animal, and get nowhere, which is
somehow satisfying anyway.

nodes.recap: campfire scene: Ef's telepathic check-in, Corolla's test [DECISION: reply on Kriss's stance], the tease, Kriss goes to sleep

dialogues.precomment:
Night falls before you've finished making the fire disappear into
dinner.# For the first time in what feels like weeks, nothing is
chasing you, nothing is bleeding, nothing is about to explode, and
you let yourself feel something close to peace.# The firelight does
something generous to Corolla's face, and to Efeliah's, and sparks
lift into the dark, carried on the warm air, or maybe on one of
Smiurl's increasingly impossible stories.##

You would give almost anything to stay exactly like this forever.#
You don't quite manage to relax anyway.# Something keeps nagging at
the edge of you, as if every stone underfoot and every stick in the
fire were humming very quietly with the same restless energy.##

Efeliah notices, even mid-laugh at one of Smiurl's jokes.
dialogues.line: Something wrong?

I can't explain it.# Do you think it's connected to that call,
whatever it is?
I don't see how it could be anything else.
dialogues.comment: Before you can say anything more, Corolla cuts in, out loud.

dialogues.line: By the way,
Hm? What is it?
dialogues.comment: You surface back into ordinary conversation.

dialogues.line: We're not staying on this beach, I take it?
Actually, I was thinking we'd leave in the morning.
Still south?

dialogues.precomment: He sounds genuinely wounded by the suggestion.
dialogues.line: Why, what's wrong with staying here?
Yes.# But why do you ask?
dialogues.comment: You don't dignify Smiurl's protest with a reply.

dialogues.line: The forest.

dialogues.precomment:
She explains, since Theo rarely bothers to finish a thought out
loud.
dialogues.line:
What he means is: skirting the forest to the east or west is one
thing.# Crossing it is another matter entirely.# We don't know
what's in there.# It could be dangerous.

replies.line: After everything I've been through, a few trees won't stop me.
I'm not thrilled either, but I'm not turning back now.

dialogues.precomment: You feel a little guilty about it anyway, and say it regardless.
dialogues.line:
After everything I've already been through, a few trees aren't
going to stop me.

dialogues.precomment: You feel a little guilty about it anyway, and say it regardless.
dialogues.line:
I'm not thrilled about it, if I'm honest.# But I'm not turning
back now.

dialogues.precomment:
Corolla studies you a moment, an odd, almost satisfied look
crossing her face, as if she'd expected exactly that answer, or
maybe its opposite, and either one would have told her something.
dialogues.line:
It was only ever to hear your opinion.# Tomorrow we cross that
forest!
dialogues.comment:
She gets to her feet and disappears into the tent you all put up
together, once the canvas had dried in the sun.

dialogues.precomment:
Theo goes on staring at the fire, unmoved.# Smiurl has started
playing with a stick and a few dying embers.# You look at Efeliah,
questioningly.
dialogues.line: So?

I think she's satisfied with you.# That she approves of your...
approach.# At least in part, certainly.
And the other part?

dialogues.precomment:
She rises and heads for the tent she shares with Corolla, and
there's a note in her voice you don't quite understand, as if she's
holding back a laugh.
dialogues.line:
Hmm.# I'm not sure.# You know they say a woman's mind is far more
complicated than a man's?
You're hiding something from me!
dialogues.comment: Smiurl looks at you like you've completely lost your mind.

dialogues.line: What makes you think that?
dialogues.comment: She's gone, into the tent, before you can come up with an answer.

dialogues.precomment:
You swallow the curiosity, kick a stone for lack of anything
better to do, and after a short, aimless walk, decide there's
nothing left to do tonight but sleep.

nodes.recap: dawn, breaking camp, heading into the forest
nodes.text:
$CYou break camp at dawn and start toward the hills to the south, and
within the first hour you understand exactly what Corolla meant.##

Vines, low branches, fallen trunks and thick undergrowth close off
your view after no more than two meters in any direction, and the
forest turns into a maze of green that gives up nothing for free.

nodes.recap: FOREST CROSSING PUZZLE - junction 1 of 2: climb costs nothing but time, guessing costs the afternoon by routing you to the adrift copy of junction 2 (115)
nodes.text:
There is no way to tell if you're still heading the right way, and
the trees are too dense at ground level to check anything by eye.

choices.desc: Send Smiurl scrambling up the tallest tree in reach.
Keep pushing forward and trust your bearings.

nodes.recap: junction 1 - climbed, on track
nodes.text:
Smiurl is up the trunk before anyone can offer to help, vanishing
into the canopy, and comes back down a minute later utterly certain
of the way.# You adjust course and press on with something like
confidence.

nodes.recap: junction 1 - guessed, forestLost gained on the choice; routes to 115, the adrift copy of junction 2, so the mistake cannot be undone for free
nodes.text:
Nobody feels like stopping to climb anything yet, so you keep
walking on instinct, choosing whichever gap in the undergrowth
looks most like a path.# More than once you have the uncomfortable
sense that a particular root or fallen log has already gone by
once before.

nodes.recap: FOREST CROSSING PUZZLE - junction 2 of 2, reached with the morning still intact; its twin is 115, reached having already guessed once
nodes.text:
The canopy opens for a moment overhead, just enough to catch the
angle of the sun before it closes again.# It's your last real
chance before midday to be sure of the way.

choices.desc: Send Smiurl up once more to fix the bearing.
Keep moving; there's no time to keep stopping.

nodes.recap: junction 2 - climbed, on track -> clean midday clearing
nodes.text:
Smiurl climbs again, and comes down nodding, satisfied.# Whatever
ground you've covered since this morning, it's the right ground.

nodes.recap: junction 1 climbed, junction 2 guessed - one mistake: you drift off a line you started the day certain of
nodes.text:
You push on without checking, and the forest quietly takes back
everything Smiurl bought you this morning.# Nothing announces it.#
The ground simply stops agreeing with the line you thought you
were walking, and by the time anyone says so out loud there is no
telling how far off it has carried you.

nodes.recap: midday clearing - both climbs made, on track
nodes.text:
By midday, exhausted, you stumble into a small natural clearing
and stop to eat, grateful for the two meters of open sky directly
above your heads.# An hour later, some strength recovered, you push
on into the trees again, well ahead of where you feared you'd be.

nodes.recap: midday clearing - one mistake, made at junction 2
nodes.text:
By midday, exhausted and more than a little frustrated, you
stumble into a small natural clearing and stop to eat, working out
between mouthfuls how much of the morning went on ground you never
needed to cover.# An hour later you push on, no more certain of
the way than you were before you stopped.

nodes.recap: arrival, on time (mid-afternoon) - both climbs made
nodes.text:
You cross the last stretch of forest at a pace that feels almost
easy after the morning, and reach the base of a rocky hill in the
mid-afternoon, with hours of good light still ahead of you.

nodes.recap: arrival, dusk - both junctions guessed
nodes.text:
The rest of the crossing costs you the afternoon along with the
morning, and by the time the trees finally start to thin around a
rocky hill, the light is already turning gold and low.# There will
be no time to waste once you're up there.

nodes.recap: arrival, late afternoon - exactly one junction guessed, whichever one it was
nodes.text:
The rest of the crossing costs you nothing you hadn't already
spent, but the morning is not coming back, and the trees thin out
around a rocky hill with the light already going long and yellow.#
There's enough of the day left to climb it, and not a great deal
more than that.

nodes.recap: FOREST CROSSING PUZZLE - junction 2, reached having already guessed at junction 1; same two options as 105, worse ground under them
nodes.text:
The canopy opens for a moment overhead, just enough to catch the
angle of the sun before it closes again.# Nobody can say how far
the morning's guessing has pulled you off the line, and this is
your last real chance before midday to find out.

choices.desc: Send Smiurl up once more to fix the bearing.
Keep moving; there's no time to keep stopping.

nodes.recap: junction 1 guessed, junction 2 climbed - one mistake, recovered late
nodes.text:
Smiurl goes up, and takes longer coming back down than he should.#
When he does, he tells it to you straight: you have drifted a good
way west of where you meant to be, and everything walked since dawn
was bought at a poor rate.# You turn onto the right line at last,
knowing exactly what it has cost to find it.

nodes.recap: both junctions guessed - the full circle
nodes.text:
You push on without checking, and it costs you.# Sometime later,
working your way around a stand of fallen trunks, you all stop
dead: they're the same trunks you climbed over an hour before.#
You've walked in a slow, complete circle, and none of you noticed.

nodes.recap: midday clearing - one mistake, made at junction 1 and corrected
nodes.text:
By midday you stumble into a small natural clearing and stop to
eat, certain of the way at last and just as certain the certainty
came late.# An hour later you push on along a bearing you actually
trust, with a good deal less daylight left to spend on it than you
would have liked.

nodes.recap: midday clearing - both junctions guessed, hopelessly lost
nodes.text:
By midday, exhausted and more than a little frustrated, you
stumble into a small natural clearing and stop to eat, all too
aware of how much of the morning you've already burned going in
circles.# An hour later you push on, no more certain of the way
than you were before you stopped.

nodes.recap: the monolith - climbing to the platform, looking back at the sea
nodes.text:
$CThe trees thin out at last around a bare, rocky summit that must
sit some two hundred meters above the sea you left behind.# A
formation of grey rock juts up from the highest point of the hill,
and you climb it, glad for once of a climb that doesn't ask you to
guess at anything, until you come out onto a kind of platform, wide
and flat enough for all five of you to stand on without anyone
risking a fall.##

With your backs to the south, you look out over the sea and the
distance you've actually covered on foot, a handful of kilometers
that took every hour of daylight you had, and privately agree it
was no small thing to manage.##

Then you turn around.

nodes.recap: the valley reveal - the white city, the siege army on cleared forest ground
nodes.text:
$CWhat greets you on the other side of the hill stops the
conversation entirely.##

A vast valley opens beneath you, running back to a wall of high
mountains, and at the bottom of it, impossibly, a city.# You can
make out the shapes of the nearest buildings past its high walls,
white in the last of the sun.# At its center a palace rises well
above everything around it, also white, ivory almost, built from
what must be marble, ringed with towers and colonnades and
porticoes and gardens.# Next to it, beautiful as the rest of the
city already is, every other building simply disappears.##

But something is wrong with the picture.# The forest that should
run right up to the northern wall has been cut down to bare ground,
and on that cleared ground an enormous army sits encamped, cookfires
scattered across it in every direction, movement everywhere you
look.# There is no mistaking what you're seeing.# That city is
under attack.# Perhaps under siege.

nodes.recap: Kriss's vision of the sack, and the certainty he must enter the city
nodes.text:
$CIt makes a kind of sense, when you think about it.# A city that
beautiful, that rich, would tempt anyone standing outside its
walls.# But you find you cannot accept the idea of it falling to
that swarm of black ants crawling under its white walls.# It
wouldn't just be a defeat.# It would be, in some way you can't
fully explain, a profanation.##

You see it happen anyway, whether you want to or not: an army a
thousand times the size of the horde that once held your companions
prisoner, pouring through those gates, moving down the loveliest
streets, carrying off statues and jewels, killing without mercy or
distinction, old, young, it wouldn't matter to them.# You see the
great palace emptied first, stripped of everything worth taking,
and then burned, left standing like the carcass of something that
used to be alive.##

And you know, with total certainty, that you have to go in.##

You have to walk those streets yourself.# Talk to whoever still
lives there.# Stand inside that palace.# Everything around you, the
pull that's been dragging at you for days, the dread that's
followed you since the beach, seems to have been pushing you toward
exactly this the whole time.# You understand it now.# You have to
reach that city.

nodes.recap: the offer and both refusals [DECISION: reply on how Kriss frames the offer] - chapter ends here

dialogues.precomment:
You say it aloud before anyone asks, because there's no point
pretending otherwise.
dialogues.line: Kriss wants to enter the city.
dialogues.comment: Theo, beside her, shakes his head.

dialogues.precomment: She gestures, taking in the whole width of the valley.
dialogues.line:
It's not possible!# How exactly do you plan to slip through that
camp unnoticed?# Look at it, it runs from one side of the valley to
the other.
dialogues.comment: Her logic is unassailable, and you know it.

dialogues.line:
I know it doesn't make sense, and that you don't understand why.#
But I know I have to go into that city.# I know now that's the
whole reason we came this far.

dialogues.precomment: As usual, he's listened to the whole exchange in silence.
dialogues.line: We're going to end up playing heroes again...
dialogues.comment: There's poorly hidden apprehension in his voice.

replies.line: Offer, but frame it as repaying a debt.

dialogues.precomment: You look straight ahead, at the city, and not at any of them.
dialogues.line: You don't need to come with me.# You've already risked enough.

dialogues.precomment: You look straight ahead, at the city, and not at any of them.
dialogues.line:
You don't have to come.# I can never repay what I already owe
you, as it is.

dialogues.precomment: She looks offended, immediately and completely.
dialogues.line:
Don't talk nonsense.# We're coming with you, wherever you decide
to go.
We won't leave you, boy.

dialogues.precomment: You look at the city a moment longer, then lower your head.
dialogues.line: Thank you.
dialogues.comment: You say it quietly, and mean every part of it.
